What the export to Jellyfin left behind

Ferrofin-only data in the database, removed from the export:
  FerrofinIntroSkipperSegments (3 rows): Intro Skipper's segments as detected and edited; those it published stay in Jellyfin's MediaSegments.
  FerrofinMeta (1 row): Ferrofin's settings for this database and the one-time repairs it ran; nothing Jellyfin needs.
  FerrofinNew (0 rows): a table of Ferrofin's own.
  _sqlx_migrations (52 rows): Ferrofin's own migration history; nothing Jellyfin needs.
  2 indexes of Ferrofin's own on Jellyfin's tables (an index holds no data of its own).

What Jellyfin will change on its first start, running the code migrations its history leaves out (the database was adopted as Jellyfin 10.11.8):
  DisableLegacyAuthorization: turns EnableLegacyAuthorization off in system.xml, so clients that sign in the legacy way stop working until it is turned on again.
  HarmonizeConflictingUserData: where one item has several play-state rows for a user that disagree, gives them all the most recently played one's values.
  UpdateNormalizedUsername: recomputes stored values from the same inputs; nothing should change.
  Before them Jellyfin copies the database (41.2 MiB) into data/SQLiteBackups, and after them it rebuilds it, so the output's volume needs about 82.4 MiB free besides the export. A start whose migrations fail restores the database from that copy and keeps the copy, one more each time.

Settings Jellyfin is not given:
  CertificatePath in config/network.xml: a path in Ferrofin's filesystem.
  Settings given to Ferrofin in config.toml, FERROFIN_* environment variables or command-line flags are not exported.

Files and stored paths:
  cache: left out of the copy; the server's cache, log or web client, which Jellyfin does not read.
  metadata: left out of the copy; not the directory the server's settings name for it.
  The metadata directory the server's settings name was not found where the export ran, so the output's metadata holds none of it: every image and folder Jellyfin looks for there through %MetadataPath% is missing. Export again where that directory is reachable at the path the settings give.
  The database's root and library rows name another data directory than the one exported: the server ran at another path, or the directory moved since. The stored paths under it were rewritten for Jellyfin too; the export printed both directories.

Backups and scheduled tasks:
  2 backup archives in data/backups made by Ferrofin, which Jellyfin cannot restore.
  Scheduled tasks: Ferrofin keeps their triggers in task_triggers.json and their last results in task_results.json, which Jellyfin does not read. Its tasks keep what its own files held before adoption, or its defaults.
